lines.text: Walk with me by the river tonight? Just the two of us.
The river's beautiful at dusk. Would you walk it with me, {player}?
I'd like an evening with you. A slow walk, nowhere to be. Come?
The river path at dusk. I'll wait by the willow.
A note, folded very carefully: "Walk with me tonight? The willow, after sunset."
A walk with you? I'd like nothing better.
Yes. I've been hoping you'd ask.
I can't tonight, I'm sorry. {when}? I'll be counting the hours.
Not tonight. Ask me {when}. Please do.
I'm not quite myself tonight. Another evening, I promise.
Not tonight. I want to be good company when we go.
Long walks aren't really my sort of evening. Could we do something else together?
A walk like that, just us? I don't think we're there, {player}. I'm sorry.
There's the willow. Shall we go downstream? The light's better that way.
Here we are. Listen to the water. Walk slowly, there's no rush tonight.
That was a bit awkward, wasn't it. We'll find our footing.
A nice walk. Thank you for tonight.
I didn't want it to end. Thank you, {player}.
I'll sleep well tonight. Let's walk again soon.
I'll remember every step of tonight. Every single one.
That was the loveliest evening of my life. I mean that.
I waited by the willow until the stars came out. You didn't come.
Our walks by the river. I find myself walking toward the willow without thinking now.
I walk past our willow and keep going. It's not the same without you.
Fireflies! All along the river! Look, there's one on your sleeve.
You took my hand on the stepping stones and didn't let go after. I noticed.
A heron lifted off the water right in front of us, silver in the last light.
The rain started and you held your jacket over us both. We didn't even hurry.
We stopped on the bridge and the whole river turned gold under us.
You picked me a flower from the bank. I'm going to press it.
We walked so far we reached the old mill. I've never been out this far with anyone.
We sat on the bank and talked until the moon came up. I lost track of everything else.
A street musician on the bridge played just for us. Well, for anyone. But it felt like us.
You told me something you've never told anyone. I'll keep it safe, I promise.
We skipped stones and laughed every time they sank. Yours sank more.
Walking back, the lanterns came on one by one, all the way home.
Lantern night on the lake? We could float one together.
Come to the lake tonight, {player}. I've made a paper lantern for us.
There's a lantern night on the water. Would you come with me?
The lake shore, after dark. I'll bring the lantern and a candle.
A note with a tiny painted lantern: "Tonight, on the lake. With me?"
Lanterns on the lake with you? Yes. Of course yes.
I'd love that. I'll write something on ours.
I can't tonight. {when}? I'll save the lantern for us.
Not tonight, sorry. {when}, if you'll still have me.
I'm too tired tonight. I want to be awake for it.
Not tonight. Another lantern night will come.
Crowds on the shore at night aren't really my thing. Could we do something quieter?
That's for people who are... together. I don't think we are, {player}.
Here's a good spot. Hold the lantern while I light it. Careful, it's paper.
Look at them all already on the water. Let's add ours.
The wind kept blowing the candle out. Maybe next time.
A pretty night. Thank you for coming.
Ours floated out so far! I'm glad we did this.
That was lovely. I keep looking back at the water.
I'll remember tonight forever. Every light on the water, and you.
I've never felt so happy. Thank you for tonight, {player}.
I floated our lantern alone. I wrote both our names on it anyway.
Our lantern nights. I keep a stack of paper ready now, for the next one.
I haven't made a lantern since we stopped going. The paper's still in the drawer.
Our lantern's drifted out further than all the others! Look, it's leading them!
We wrote our wishes on it and didn't show each other. I'll tell you mine one day.
The lights are reflected in the water so it looks like two skies. One above, one below.
A breeze pushed our lantern back to the shore, right to us. Like it didn't want to leave.
Someone on a boat started singing and the whole shore joined in.
You shielded the candle with your hands so it wouldn't go out. It didn't.
We sat on the shore until the last lantern went out. Then we stayed a bit longer.
A fish jumped right through the reflection of our lantern. It scattered into a hundred lights.
The fireworks started over the far shore just as ours touched the water.
You leaned on my shoulder and we watched the water without a word.
Ichiraku tonight? I'm starving, and I hate eating ramen alone.
I'd kill for a bowl of miso ramen. Come with me, {player}? I'll get the eggs.
The broth smells reached my window an hour ago. Ramen? Please say ramen.
Ramen at Ichiraku tonight, if you're free. I'll keep the stool by the end warm.
A note, folded small: "Ichiraku, after sundown? Bring an appetite."
Ramen? Always. Let's go before the queue gets long.
Yes! I've been thinking about pork broth since breakfast.
I can't right now, I'm stuck with work. {when}, though? I'd love a bowl then.
Not today, I've got a shift. Ask me again {when}.
I'm not hungry, oddly. Another day, {player}.
Ramen sounds good, but not tonight. I'm worn out.
I'm sorry, I've never been much for ramen. Too heavy for me.
Ramen together? That's kind, but I barely know you yet.
Two bowls, please! Extra pork in one. You know which.
Here we are. Sit on the left, the right stool wobbles.
Well. The noodles were good, at least. Let's not do this again too soon.
That hit the spot. Thanks for coming along.
I'm so full I might roll home. That was lovely, {player}.
Good bowl, good company. Same again sometime?
Best bowl I've had all year, and I think it's because of the company. Let's do this forever.
I haven't laughed like that in ages. Ramen's better with you, {player}.
I sat at Ichiraku with two bowls going cold. Where were you, {player}?
Our ramen nights. That's a thing now, isn't it? I like that it's a thing.
The cook asked where my friend was. I didn't know what to say. Our ramen's been missing.
The bowl's tipping! ...You caught it! Not a drop spilled!
The cook just gave us both a free egg for "looking so hungry." I'll take it!
We slurped at exactly the same time and the whole counter turned round. Ha!
You got broth on your nose. No, other side. No... here, let me.
A second bowl? You're mad. ...Make it two.
It's raining on the curtain and we're all warm in here. I could stay all night.
Did you just win the noodle-pulling bet against the cook? You did! Legendary!
You split your last piece of pork with me. That's real friendship, that is.
I've never noticed how many stars there are over the stand. Look up.
The cook told us the story of the first bowl they ever made. Burnt, apparently!
A stray cat sat between our stools and stared at us the whole time. We've been adopted.
We talked so long the cook started stacking stools around us. Oops.
Dango at the tea house? They've got the three-colour ones today.
I'd love a sweet skewer and a quiet cup. Join me, {player}?
Let's go for dango. My treat, if you promise not to eat mine.
Tea house this afternoon? I'll order the mitarashi before you get there.
Dango and green tea, by the river window, if you'd like to meet.
Dango! Yes. I'll even share the sauce.
That sounds lovely. Let's sit by the window.
I'm tied up just now. Could we go {when}?
I've errands until late. {when}, maybe? I'll save my appetite.
I've had too many sweets already this week. Another time.
Not today, {player}. I'm not in a tea house mood.
I don't have much of a sweet tooth, I'm afraid. Dango's not for me.
That's sweet of you. Maybe once we know each other a little better.
Two plates of dango and a pot of tea, please. The window seat's free!
Here we are. Smell that? They've just brushed the fresh ones.
That was a bit quiet, wasn't it. The dango was nice, anyway.
Good tea, good dango. Thanks, {player}.
I feel sweet all the way through. Thank you, that was nice.
Let's come back here. It's a good spot for us.
I'm going to remember this afternoon. Sun, tea, sticky fingers and you.
That was perfect. The kind of afternoon people write poems about.
I ate both plates of dango waiting for you. I didn't even enjoy the second.
Our dango afternoons. The tea seller pours two cups the moment we walk in now.
I walked past the tea house today and didn't go in. It's ours. It didn't feel right alone.
The sparrows are stealing crumbs from our plate! Look at that brave one!
You got the skewer with four balls instead of three. That's lucky, you know.
Sauce on your chin. And your sleeve. And somehow your hair. Impressive.
A petal fell right into my tea. That's got to mean something good.
The tea master gave us a taste of the special blend. I feel very grown up.
We sat here so long the shadows moved right across the table.
You made me laugh so hard I snorted tea. Out of my NOSE, {player}.
A little one at the next table waved at us the whole time. So we waved back the whole time.
We tried every colour of dango they had. Seven! I'm never eating again.
Rain started and we stayed, listening to it on the roof. Best part of the day.
Barbecue tonight? I've been craving grilled beef all week.
Let's get a grill and a pile of meat, {player}. My stomach's demanding it.
The barbecue house has a free table at seven. Come with me?
Barbecue tonight? I'll start the grill. You bring the hunger.
A table at the barbecue house, after dark. I've booked for us.
Barbecue! You're speaking my language.
Yes. I'll man the tongs. You stay back from the fire.
I can't tonight. Could we go {when}? I'll be twice as hungry by then.
Busy till late, I'm afraid. {when} instead?
I've already eaten, sadly. Another night.
Not tonight. The smoke gets in my eyes when I'm tired.
Grilled meat and smoke? Not really for me. Sorry.
A whole evening at the barbecue? Let's get to know each other a bit first.
Grill's hot! Beef first, then the onions. Trust me on the onions.
Here we are. Sit on this side, the smoke drifts the other way.
That got a bit awkward, didn't it. Well, the meat was good.
Good food. I smell like a bonfire now. Worth it.
I'm stuffed. That was a proper feast, {player}. Thank you.
Same table next time? I'm already looking forward to it.
That was a feast for the ages. I'll be telling people about tonight.
I can't remember the last time I laughed this much with my mouth full.
I grilled for two and ate for two, alone. Thanks for nothing, {player}.
Barbecue night, you and me. It's tradition now. Don't argue.
The barbecue house keeps our table empty out of habit. I've stopped going.
The flames jumped and singed your eyebrow! Just one! You look so surprised!
You flipped every piece perfectly. Not one burnt. Who taught you that?
The owner sent over a plate of the special cut, on the house. We must look trustworthy.
Ha! We reached for the last piece at the same time. Rock, paper, scissors for it?
The whole table next to us joined in our toast. Everyone's cheering!
I ate so much I had to undo my sash. Don't look. Okay, look, it's funny.
You let me have the crispy bits. You're a true friend, {player}.
We stayed till the coals went orange and low. That's the best part.
A spark landed on your sleeve and you put it out without even stopping talking. Ha!
The grill master taught us the secret sauce! Well, half of it. The other half's a family secret.
Come to dinner at mine tonight? Nothing fancy. Just rice, fish and us.
I'd like you to eat at my table, {player}. Tonight, if you can.
I'm cooking tonight and I always make too much. Come and help me eat it.
Dinner at my house tonight. Come hungry, and don't bring anything. I mean it.
A note: "Supper at mine. Six bells. Your place is already set."
Dinner at yours? I'd love that. I'll be there on time.
Thank you. I'll bring a good appetite.
I'm busy this evening. Could you come {when} instead?
Tonight's no good, sadly. {when}? I'll cook something special.
The house is a mess tonight. Another evening, {player}.
Not tonight. I'm too tired to cook, and I won't feed you leftovers.
I don't really have people over. I'm sorry. Let's eat out instead some time.
At my home? I don't have many people over. Maybe when we're closer.
Welcome! Mind the low beam. Everyone hits it once.
Come in, shoes there. Sit, sit. The soup's nearly ready.
Well. That was a little stiff, wasn't it. Thank you for coming all the same.
Thank you for coming. It was nice to cook for someone.
That was a warm evening. You're welcome back any night.
You ate everything! That's the best compliment a cook can get.
That felt like family. Like you'd always been at that table.
I'll remember tonight. All of us round the table, and you right in the middle of it.
I set the table for you. The rice went cold. Everyone kept looking at the door.
You've got your own bowl at my house now. It lives on the shelf, waiting for you.
Your bowl's still on my shelf. It hasn't been used in weeks.
You've got your own bowl now. I bought it this week. It's got a little leaf on it.
The little ones made you a seat cushion. It's lumpy. They're so proud.
The rice came out perfect, every grain shining. I never manage that! You're lucky.
My grandmother told her ghost story, the one about the fox, and you jumped! Ha!
We all cleared the table together and sang the washing-up song. You learned it so fast.
The power of the hot pot! Everyone's cheeks are red and nobody can stop smiling.
The cat climbed into your lap and fell asleep. It's never done that with anyone.
You helped me fold the dumplings. Yours look like little hats. I love them.
Second helpings, third helpings! The pot's empty. That's never happened in this house.
We stayed up talking by the brazier after everyone else went to bed.
The neighbours heard us laughing and came over with sweets. The whole lane's here now!
My father toasted you at the table. He never toasts anyone. He meant it.
I've got Academy homework. Loads of it. {when}? Ask me then!
My mum says you can come for dinner tonight. She's making the good fish. Come!
I can't tonight. My big cousins are visiting and there's no room at the table.
I don't really like having friends over. My house is boring. Can we go somewhere else?
My mum only lets real friends come for dinner. Maybe later, okay?
That was nice. My mum says you've got good manners.
You didn't come to dinner! My mum made extra and everything.
Look, my mum got you your own bowl! It's got a leaf on it! It's yours now!
My dad let us roll the rice balls ourselves. Yours is shaped like a cat!
That was okay. I got all wrinkly.
We haven't been to the bathhouse in ages. I miss the cold milk after.
Fishing at dawn? The river's high and the trout are hungry.
I've a spare rod, {player}. Come sit by the river with me a while.
Let's go fishing. We don't even have to catch anything. Just sit.
River at first light. I'll bring the bait, you bring the patience.
A note tucked in your door: "Fishing tomorrow, early. The flat rock by the bend."
Fishing? Yes. Quiet water's just what I need.
I'll dig up some worms. Meet you at the bend.
I'm busy this morning. {when}? The fish will wait.
Can't today. Try me {when}, early.
The river's too muddy after the rain. Another day.
Not today. I couldn't sit still if I tried.
Sitting still for hours waiting for a fish? I'd go mad. Sorry.
Fishing's my quiet time. Maybe when we know each other better.
Here's the spot. Cast past the reeds, and then just... wait.
Mist on the water. Perfect. Quiet now, or you'll scare them off.
Not a nibble, and not much to say either. Oh well.
Two small ones and a sunburn. A fair morning.
That was peaceful. I didn't think about anything for hours. Thank you.
Good catch, good company. Let's come back.
That was the best morning I've had in a long time. The river, the quiet, you.
I'm going to remember this morning when things get loud.
I fished alone until noon. Caught one. Talked to it about you. It didn't care either.
Our fishing mornings. The flat rock at the bend is ours now, as far as I'm concerned.
Our rock at the river's been empty for weeks. Somebody else sat on it. I glared.
A big one! Pull, {player}, pull! ...We got it! Look at the size of it!
A heron landed right next to us and fished better than both of us combined.
You fell in! Right in! Come here, I'll pull you out. Stop laughing, you'll swallow the river.
The sun's coming up through the mist. Look at the water. It's on fire.
We caught the same fish on both our lines! How is that even possible?
An otter's watching us from the other bank. I think it wants our bait.
We just sat in silence for an hour, and it was the best conversation we've had.
You caught a sandal. A whole sandal! Someone in the village is walking around with one.
We grilled our catch right here on the bank. Nothing's ever tasted this good.
You let the little one go. "Come back bigger," you said. I liked that.
Stargazing on the Hokage Rock tonight? The sky's going to be clear.
Come up the Rock with me after dark. I want to show you a constellation.
It's a clear night. Let's lie on the Rock and count shooting stars.
The Hokage Rock, after dark. I'll bring a blanket and tea.
A note: "Clear skies tonight. Meet me on top of the Rock. Look up."
Stars? Yes. I'll bring the warm tea.
I'd love that. Let's go before the moon rises and washes them out.
Not tonight, I've an early start. {when}, if it's clear?
I'm busy after dark tonight. How about {when}?
The clouds are coming in. We'd see nothing. Another night.
I'm too tired to climb the Rock tonight. Soon, though.
Lying on cold rock staring at dots? Not for me, sorry.
Up on the Rock at night, just us? Maybe once we know each other better.
Lie back. No, further. There. Now look straight up.
Here, blanket. The stone's cold. Now give your eyes a minute.
Clouds rolled in, and so did the awkward silence. Ah well.
A clear patch, a few stars. Not bad for a weeknight.
I always feel small up there. Small in a good way. Thanks for coming.
That was lovely. Let's do it again when the sky's this clear.
I've never seen the sky like that. And I've never wanted to share it with anyone before.
That was magic, {player}. I'm still dizzy from all the stars.
I lay on the Rock and watched the stars alone. There were a lot of them. I counted.
Our nights on the Rock. I've named a star after them. Not after you. After the nights.
I haven't been up the Rock at night in weeks. It doesn't feel the same alone.
A shooting star! Did you see it? Make a wish, quick!
That cluster there looks just like a ramen bowl. You see it too? The Ramen! We've named one!
The whole village's lanterns are going out one by one below us. Like it's falling asleep.
Three shooting stars in a row! That's three wishes. Don't waste them.
You fell asleep mid-sentence. I let you. The stars were keeping watch anyway.
An owl landed on the stone head right above us. It's watching us watch the sky.
The Milky Way's so bright tonight. It looks like spilt rice across the dark.
We stayed up until the sky went grey. We watched the whole night turn.
We both pointed at the same star at the same time. Of all of them.
You told me the story your teacher told about the stars. I'd never heard it. I love it.
Come paint with me at the overlook? You don't have to be good. I'm not.
I've got spare brushes and a whole roll of paper. Paint the valley with me?
The light's lovely at the overlook today. Let's go and paint it.
The overlook, midday. I'll set up two easels.
A note, with a little ink drawing of a tree: "Paint with me tomorrow?"
Painting? I'd love to. I'll try not to get ink on your sleeves.
Yes. I'll bring the good paper.
I'm busy today. {when}? The view will keep.
Not right now. {when}, when the light's better?
I'm not feeling creative today. Everything I paint would be grey.
The wind's too strong at the overlook today. Another time.
Painting? I can't draw a straight line. I'd just be embarrassed.
I don't paint in front of people I don't know well. It's too personal.
There. The whole valley. Don't paint what you see, paint what you feel. Or both.
Water, ink, brush. Start with the sky. It's the easiest to get wrong.
Neither of us got anything down that we liked. Oh well. Ink washes off.
A few decent sketches. A nice way to pass the afternoon.
Look at yours! You've got a feel for it. I'm a little jealous.
That was peaceful. I'll pin today's painting by my door.
Today I painted the best thing I've ever painted, and I think it's because you were here.
That was wonderful. Let's swap paintings. I want yours.
I set up two easels at the overlook. I painted the empty one, in the end.
Our painting afternoons. I've a whole folder of your work now. Don't ask for it back.
My brushes have gone stiff. I haven't been to the overlook since we stopped going.
A gust took your painting right off the easel! It's flying over the valley! Bye!
You painted me! When? That's me, isn't it? It's lovely!
A rainbow's come out over the valley, right where we're painting. Quick, quick!
We both painted the same cloud, in completely different colours. Yours is purple!
A little deer walked right up to the easels to see what we were doing.
You knocked the inkpot over and made the best accidental mountain I've ever seen.
A passing merchant offered to buy your painting! Five ryo! Sell it! Don't sell it!
We painted until the light went, and then we painted the dusk.
A game of shogi at the tea house? I promise not to gloat. Much.
I've been studying openings. Play me, {player}? I need a victim.
Shogi this afternoon? Loser pays for the tea.
Shogi at the tea house this afternoon. I'll set up the board.
A note: "I challenge you to shogi. Tea house. Bring your best defence."
Shogi? Yes. Prepare to lose your rook.
Gladly. It's been ages since I had a real opponent.
I can't right now. {when}? I'll be sharper then.
Busy today. Play me {when}.
My head's too full to think three moves ahead. Another day.
Not today. I'd play badly and blame you.
Shogi bores me, I'm afraid. All that sitting and staring.
I'm particular about who I play. Let's get to know each other first.
Board's set. You move first. Think carefully.
Tea's poured, pieces are out. Begin when you're ready.
That game went sideways, and so did the conversation. Next time.
A decent game. Neither of us disgraced ourselves.
Good game. You made me think. That doesn't happen often.
I'll be replaying that game in my head all night. Well played.
That was the best game I've played in a year. I'd frame the board if I could.
Brilliant. Every move a conversation. Let's play again soon.
I set up the board and played both sides. I lost. To myself. Where were you?
Our shogi games. The tea house keeps our board in the corner now.
Our board's been gathering dust in the tea house corner. The owner asked if you'd quit.
A draw! Perfectly balanced! Nobody can move! That never happens!
You took my king with a lowly pawn. A pawn! I'll never live that down.
A crowd's gathered round our board. Old players, nodding. I'm sweating.
That trap you set took twenty moves to spring. Twenty! I didn't see it at all.
The old champion at the next table leaned over and said "good move" to you. To YOU.
We played so long the tea went cold three times.
I knocked the board with my elbow and we had to rebuild it from memory. And we did!
You let me take back one move. Just one. I'm grateful and humiliated.
Your comeback, from three pieces down! I had you! How did I not have you?
We invented a new opening by accident. We should name it after ourselves.
Study with me at the Academy library? I've a scroll I can't make sense of alone.
The library's quiet this afternoon. Come read with me, {player}?
Let's go to the library. I need someone to stop me falling asleep on the desk.
Academy library, after lunch. I'll save the table by the window.
A note in very neat writing: "Library tomorrow? I've found a scroll you'll like."
The library? Yes. I've three scrolls I want to finish.
Gladly. Two heads are better than one for those old scrolls.
I'm busy just now. {when}? The scrolls won't run away.
Can't today. {when}, maybe?
My eyes are too tired for reading today. Another time.
Not today. My brain's full.
Sitting in a library all afternoon? I'd fall asleep in minutes. Sorry.
I'm a bit private when I study. Maybe once we know each other better.
Shh. Window table's free. I'll get the scrolls, you get the ink.
Here. Mind the librarian, they hear everything.
We didn't get much done, and we got shushed twice. Oh well.
Productive afternoon. My hand aches from notes.
I understand it now! You explained it better than the scroll did.
Good study session. Let's make a habit of it.
That was the best afternoon of study I've ever had. I actually enjoyed it!
I feel twice as clever. Let's do this every week.
I saved the window table all afternoon. The librarian kept giving me pitying looks.
Our library afternoons. The librarian sets out two cushions for us now.
I've been studying alone again. The window table feels very big.
We found a pressed flower inside an old history scroll. Someone hid it there years ago.
We both laughed at the same line and the librarian shushed us so hard a candle went out.
You solved the riddle in the margin! The one nobody's solved! Write your name next to it!
A scroll fell off the top shelf right onto your head. Are you all right? It's about falling objects!
The librarian showed us the oldest scroll in the Academy. We weren't allowed to touch it. We breathed on it.
Rain against the window, a pile of scrolls and nowhere to be. Perfect.
You fell asleep on my notes and woke up with my writing on your cheek. Backwards!
We found a map of the village from before the Academy was built. Everything's in the wrong place!
The blossoms are out in the flower park! Come and sit under them with me?
Flower viewing, {player}? I'll pack a lunch box. You bring a mat.
The cherry trees won't last the week. Let's see them while they're perfect.
Flower park, midday. I've claimed a spot under the biggest tree.
A note with a petal pressed inside: "Blossoms are out. Come and look with me."
Flower viewing? Oh, yes. I've been waiting all year.
I'd love to. I'll make sweet rice cakes for under the trees.
I'm busy today. {when}? Let's hope the petals hold.
Can't right now. {when}, before they fall?
The pollen's making me sneeze. Another day.
It's too windy today. The petals are all blowing off.
Sitting under trees looking at flowers? Not really my thing. Sorry.
A whole afternoon under the blossoms? Let's know each other better first.
Mat down, shoes off. Now look up. Isn't it something?
Here's our spot. Pink above, pink below. Sit, sit.
Crowded, windy, and we didn't have much to say. The flowers were pretty, though.
A pleasant afternoon under the trees. Thank you.
I'm covered in petals and I don't mind at all. Lovely day, {player}.
That was so peaceful. Let's do it every spring.
That was the most beautiful afternoon. I'll think of it every spring for the rest of my life.
Petals, sunshine, sweet rice and you. I couldn't ask for more.
I sat under the blossoms alone all afternoon. They fell on the empty half of the mat.
Our flower viewing. The same tree every spring. It's ours now.
Our tree's in bloom and we haven't been. It feels like a waste of a whole spring.
A petal landed right in your cup! That's good luck for a whole year!
A gust shook the tree and it's snowing blossoms all over us! Look!
The families on the next mat shared their sweets with us. Everyone's so happy today.
You've got petals in your hair. Don't brush them out. They suit you.
We fell asleep under the tree and woke up covered in pink. Like a blanket!
An old couple played the flute under the next tree. We just listened, all afternoon.
We tried catching falling petals. You caught three! I caught a leaf.
The lanterns came on in the park as we were leaving. The blossoms glowed.
It's boiling. Swim in the lake with me? Last one in's a soggy rice cake!
Let's go swimming, {player}. The lake's perfect this time of year.
The lake! Today! I'll race you to the rock in the middle.
The lake, after lunch. Bring a towel and a brave face, the water's cold at first.
A note, a bit damp: "Swim tomorrow? Meet at the jetty."
A swim? Yes, please. I'm melting.
Let's go! I'll race you to the jetty.
I'm busy today. {when}? It'll still be hot.
Can't right now. {when} works.
I've a cold coming on. Better not.
Not today. The water's choppy and I'm tired.
I'm not much of a swimmer, honestly. I'll sit this one out.
Swimming together? Let's get to know each other first.
Here's the jetty. Count of three. One... two... I'm already in!
The water's lovely! Well, it's cold. Then it's lovely. Get in!
Cold water, cold mood. We'll try again on a warmer day.
